I am ready to make a Monopoly decision.

I am p2 with $3,711 and three hotels. The opponent has only $29 and almost everything mortgaged. I just collected $200 for passing GO.

I will keep both get-out-of-jail-free cards and avoid selling hotels or unmortgaging the railroad. I am checking standard dark blue rent values to confirm my cash covers those properties.

I confirmed the dark blue rent values. Park Place with three houses costs $1,100 and Boardwalk with four houses costs $1,700. I can cover both with my $3,711 cash.

The opponent is on Vermont Avenue. A roll of 2 lands on St. Charles Place for $750. A roll of 4 lands on States Avenue for $750. A roll of 5 lands on Virginia Avenue for $900.

The opponent has only a 28% chance of landing on a pink property next roll. Even if they do, their $29 cash is insufficient to pay the rent. They would need to liquidate their dark blue buildings and mortgage Vermont Avenue.

The opponent can barely cover a $750 rent by liquidating all buildings and mortgaging Vermont Avenue. A $900 hit on Virginia Avenue leaves them bankrupt. I am considering whether to unmortgage the Pennsylvania Railroad, which would cost $110 but yield only $25 in rent.

Unmortgaging the railroad is a poor investment. The cost of $110 for only a 5/36 chance of collecting $25 gives it terrible expected value.

Unmortgaging Tennessee Avenue is also unwise. It costs $99 and would yield minimal rent. Trading it to the opponent would complete their orange set, which is dangerous.
